record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For pure bipartite-state transformations under local quantum operations and classical communication, Nielsen’s majorization criterion decides when one state A can be converted to another state B. Because some conversions become possible only after tensoring both states with a suitable entangled catalyst C, give an efficient criterion for deciding when there exists a catalyst C such that A tensor C can be converted to B tensor C.

evidence.quote: Using Nielsen’s criterion one can show [JP1] that the following strange situation can happen: state A cannot be converted to state B, but A ⊗ C can be converted to B ⊗ C, where C is a suitably chosen entangled state, the ”catalyst”.
The problem is to give a similarly efficient criterion to decide which pure bipartite states can be converted into each other using a catalyst.

Thus we would like to characterize the order relation “catalytic majorization”:
For some r, (p⊗r) is more mixed than (q ⊗r) in the sense of majorization.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p = (p_1, \dots, p_n)$ and $q = (q_1, \dots, q_n)$ be probability vectors with entries in non-increasing order. Recall that $p$ is majorized by $q$, written $p \prec q$, if $\sum_{i=1}^k p_i \le \sum_{i=1}^k q_i$ for all $1 \le k \le n-1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i = \sum_{i=1}^n q_i$. By Nielsen's theorem, a pure bipartite quantum state with Schmidt-coefficient-squared vector $q$ can be deterministically converted to one with Schmidt-coefficient-squared vector $p$ using local operations and classical communication if and only if $p \prec q$.

Say that $p$ is catalytically majorized by $q$, written $p \prec_T q$, if there exists some integer $r \ge 1$ and a probability vector $c = (c_1, \dots, c_r)$ such that
$$ p \otimes c \;\prec\; q \otimes c, $$
where $p \otimes c$ denotes the probability vector with entries $p_i c_j$ arranged in non-increasing order (and similarly for $q \otimes c$).

Problem: Give an efficient (in particular, decidable in finitely many steps as a function of $n$) necessary-and-sufficient criterion, in terms of $p$ and $q$ alone, for whether $p \prec_T q$ holds.
artifact.status_search_result: Klimesh and Turgut independently characterized catalytic majorization by an infinite family of Rényi-entropy inequalities (all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$), and the IQOQI Open Quantum Problems page lists the problem as solved on this basis. However, Gour and others showed that for $d \ge 4$ no finite set of conditions on $p,q$ can be necessary and sufficient, so a strictly finite/efficient criterion in the original sense does not exist; recent work (2025) provides finite sufficient (but not necessary) conditions. Hence the problem is best described as partially solved: characterized by infinite inequalities, with finite necessary-and-sufficient criteria provably impossible in general.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic majorization – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: A complete solution was independently obtained by Klimesh and Turgut.
status_evidence.claim: The catalytic majorization order is characterized by Rényi entropy inequalities.

status_evidence.title: A finite sufficient set of conditions for catalytic majorization
status_evidence.snippet: We derive a finite sufficient set of inequalities implying catalysis.
status_evidence.claim: Finite necessary-and-sufficient conditions are impossible for d≥4; only finite sufficient conditions are known.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Majorization and ℓ_p Norms
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of catalytic majorization in terms of ℓ_p norms / Rényi entropies.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization requires checking infinitely many inequalities.
